header: How I read a vehicle identification number (VIN): "MALBM51BLKM000001" -> world manufacturer MAL (Hyundai Motor India), the maker's own descriptor BM51B, position 9 L (not a check digit: Indian makers use it for their own code), model year K (2019), plant M, serial 000001. Pure; nothing is stored or sent anywhere. The structure is ISO 3779 (the 17 characters) and ISO 3780 (the World Manufacturer Identifier, which SAE International assigns); the letters I, O and Q are never used, so that nothing is mistaken for 1 or 0. Positions 1-3 are the WMI, 4-9 the Vehicle Descriptor Section (VDS), 10-17 the Vehicle Indicator Section (VIS). The check digit of position 9 (a weighted sum modulo 11) is required in North America and is NOT used by Indian makers. What a maker puts in positions 4-8, the plant letter and the month is the maker's own business: my reader says only what the standard fixes, names the manufacturer and plant only where I am sure, and says plainly when a part is the maker's own code. The vehicle's papers (registration certificate, invoice) and the maker are the authority. Indian chassis plates: Hyundai stamps the VIN followed by "*" and a letter for the month of manufacture (MALBM51BLKM000001*L: L = November); I read that suffix and guess nothing else. WHOSE NUMBERS I READ (my rule of 26 Nov 2026, widened on 27 Nov): the makers whose cars are sold in India, and for each only the manufacturer code it uses in INDIA. Twenty buttons: the five Indian makers (Hyundai Motor India, Kia India, Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, Mahindra) and, at the owner's request, Honda, Toyota, Nissan, Volkswagen, Škoda, Renault and Citroën, and (28 Nov) Jeep, Mercedes-Benz, Fiat and Ford (the last two have a `remark`: their new cars are no longer sold in India, which I checked first: Ford's own statement of 9 Sep 2021 and Business Standard of 18 Mar 2025; reports of May 2026 that Fiat has announced no return). The owner also asked for Volvo, BYD, Audi and BMW, but no source I could read gives a manufacturer code for their cars made or sold in India (the compiled list has only BMW's motorcycles made by TVS, WB3, and Volvo Eicher's commercial vehicles, MC2, which are not those cars), so they were NOT here at first. The owner then decided (28 Nov): where no source gives an Indian code, give the INTERNATIONAL code with a clear declaration. So Audi (WAU, WA1), BMW (WBA, WBS, WBX, WBY), Volvo (YV1, YV4) and BYD (LGX, LC0) are here, each named in the compiled list and by NHTSA's vPIC, each marked `scope: international`: the code is the maker's anywhere in the world, the country shown is the code's, and nothing says where this car was built. A code is never guessed. A code stays in the list only when a source names it for that maker: Maruti's own customer page (MA3) and Renault India's own page (MEE) say it themselves; for the others a compiled manufacturer-code list names it (Wikibooks' World Manufacturer Identifier list, read on 27 Nov 2026) and, where I found one, a second source. Each entry says which (`basis`). BIS, the Indian coordinator of the WMI, holds the official register; SAE International assigns the codes and the register is not published, so no source I could read is "the" register. The codes of positions 4 to 8 of every maker are the maker's own and none of them publishes them, so for none do I pretend to decode them; dealer guides that give a month or a model at some position (for Volkswagen, Tata, Mahindra) I could not confirm from a maker, and I do not use them.

symbols.name: MAKERS
symbols.sig: const MAKERS: Array<{ id: "hyundai" | "kia" | "maruti" | "tata" | "mahindra" | "honda" | "toyota" | "nissan" | "volkswagen" | "skoda" | "renault" | "citroen" | "jeep" | "mercedes" | "fiat" | "ford" | "audi" | "bmw" | "volvo" | "byd"; button: string; maker: string; wmi: string; alsoWmi?: string[]; sample: string; note: string; remark?: string; more?: true }> = [ { id: "hyundai", button: "Hyundai In
doc: THE MAKERS, one button each under the number box: the first four are chips of their own; the rest (`more`, Mahindra first) are in the dropdown of the FIFTH chip, which shows Mahindra until another is chosen and then shows the maker chosen (one row of five, whatever the number of makers). Hyundai Motor India and Kia India are TWO: they hold different manufacturer codes and are two companies, and I found no document that says their positions 4 to 8 follow one code. Volkswagen and Škoda are two buttons too (the owner asked for both), but they share ONE code, MEX, issued to one company, so the code cannot tell the two brands apart and the notes say so. `note` says only what a source states; it is shown under the reading of a number of that maker. `alsoWmi` lists a further code listed for the same maker.

doc: The state of position 9. "valid": a check digit that matches; "mismatch": a digit or X that does not match; "none": a letter, so no check digit.

doc: One line of the answer to the question users bring to a VIN: is the manufacturing YEAR (or MONTH) in this number? `state` is said in bold on the card, YES or NO.

members.name: remark
doc: the maker's remark (its new cars are no longer sold in India), or null

members.name: warnings
doc: Worries that do not stop me from reading the number (a position-10 code that is never a year).

behaviours: known numbers get their known check digit: 1HGBH41JXMN109186 is X, 5YJSA1DG9DFP14705 is 9, 1M8GDM9AXKP042788 is X, all ones is 1
the steps are shown: 17 positions, position 9 has weight 0, the sum modulo 11 is the digit (10 is X)
the likely year is the latest one that is not later than next year: K is 2019, V is 2027 in 2026 but 1997 in 2024, 3 is 2003
a Hyundai India number is read part by part: country, manufacturer, descriptor, position 9, year, plant, serial
M with A is India, MAL is Hyundai Motor India
position 9 L is a letter: not a check digit, Indian makers use it for their own code
K is 2019 (or 1989); the plant letter M is Hyundai's Sriperumbudur plant; the descriptor is the maker's own
the facts: 17 characters, India, 2019, check digit not used
the plate may carry Hyundai's month letter after a star: *L is November, the stamped number is 19 characters
the month letters of Hyundai: A January ... H August, J September, K October, L November, M December (no I)
an extension on another maker's number is not guessed
an American number with a right check digit says it is right
a wrong check digit in North America is a probable typing mistake, and says what it should be
outside North America a digit that does not match is not called an error
the wrong length is said: 16 typed, none typed, 11 (before 1981)
I, O and Q are refused with the likely digit: I as 1, O and Q as 0
a character that is not a letter or digit is refused
a year code that is never one gives a warning but the rest is still read
an unknown manufacturer code is said to be unknown, not guessed
spaces, hyphens and lower case are ignored; a word like VIN or chassis number in front is taken off
a line is taken for a VIN, as you type, only when it is one: 17 valid characters, letters and digits, a possible year code; or when it says vin
regions: M is Asia, MA-ME India; 1, 4, 5 United States; J Japan; W Germany; KM South Korea; S UK; Z Italy

the codes listed are exactly these twenty-six: sixteen issued for India and ten international (Audi, BMW, Volvo, BYD), each naming its company: the five Indian makers, then Honda, Toyota, Nissan, Škoda Auto Volkswagen, Renault, Citroën, FCA India (Jeep), Mercedes-Benz India, Fiat India, Ford India; no foreign maker's own code (KMH, JHM, WVW, TMB ...) and no code of another Indian company I was not asked for (MEC BharatBenz, WB3 BMW motorcycles, MC2 Volvo Eicher)
the full forms: VIN, WMI, VDS, VIS, the two ISO standards, SAE
the three sections cover positions 1 to 17 without a gap or an overlap
the samples are all readable, and none is a real vehicle's (serial 000001, made up)

there are twenty makers: four with a chip of their own (Hyundai India, Kia India, Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors) and sixteen in the dropdown of the fifth chip, which is Mahindra's until another is chosen: Mahindra, Honda, Toyota, Nissan, Volkswagen, Škoda, Renault, Citroën, Jeep, Mercedes-Benz, Fiat, Ford, Audi, BMW, Volvo, BYD; the samples carry the names of the buttons
every sample is a number of its own maker (its first three characters are the maker's manufacturer code) and is read as that maker
Hyundai and Kia are two buttons with two different manufacturer codes (MAL and MZB), and the Kia reading says that no document ties its positions 4 to 8 to Hyundai's
a Kia number is read as India although MZB lies outside the MA-ME range: the country comes from the list, and the reading says so
Maruti's note is its own words (MA3 followed by 14 letters and digits); Tata's and Mahindra's say that what follows the code is the maker's own
only Hyundai's plant letter is named (Sriperumbudur, M); no other maker's plant is guessed
the descriptor of every one of the five is said to be the maker's own, never decoded
the Hyundai month letter says how sure it is (guides and owners; no Hyundai document found); a Kia number with a star is not read for a month
each of the eleven with an Indian code has it: Honda MAK, Toyota MBJ, Nissan MDH, Volkswagen and Škoda MEX, Renault MEE, Citroën MZZ, Jeep MCA, Mercedes-Benz MBR, Fiat MAH, Ford MAJ

Jeep's note says MCA is the company's code for Fiat as well, so the code cannot tell the two apart, and that no maker document and no second source was found; Mercedes-Benz's says the same of its code and that BharatBenz trucks have another
every sample of the eleven with an Indian code is made up (serial 000001, a letter in position 9 so no check digit is shown, P = 2023, no I, O or Q) and is read as its maker, in India
Citroën's MZZ lies outside MA-ME, like Kia's MZB: the country comes from the list and the reading says so
Volkswagen and Škoda are two buttons and one code, one company: the notes say that MEX alone cannot tell the two brands apart

the basis of each code is told: Maruti's MA3 and Renault's MEE are on the maker's own page, all the others in compiled lists; Renault's note quotes its page (17 characters starting with MEE, on the registration certificate or at the bottom of the windscreen)

what no source gave is said, not filled in: Toyota's and Citroën's notes say no maker document prints the code; Nissan's that its VIN page gives no layout; Honda's rests on the lists and on court orders
none of the seven is decoded beyond the standard: the descriptor is the maker's own, the plant is not named, no month is read from a star
Hyundai's second code MB2 (listed for its SUVs) is read as Hyundai Motor India with Hyundai's note; its month letter is read for MAL only, because no source says the plate of an MB2 car is the same
a ready-built import carries its foreign maker's code, which is not in the list and is said to be unknown (a Škoda of the Czech plants, TMB; a Toyota of Japan, JTD)
the last chip is a dropdown of my own: a listbox with arrow keys, Home, End, Escape and a click outside, opening to the left when there is no room; its label becomes the maker chosen
the row is five items: four chips and one split chip (name + chevron), never a sixth button; the fifth shows Mahindra at the start and the maker chosen afterwards
the four with international codes: Audi WAU (WA1), BMW WBA (WBS, WBX, WBY), Volvo YV1 (YV4), BYD LGX (LC0), in the dropdown after Mercedes-Benz

the declaration is made on the reading: each of the four says its code is international, that no source gives an Indian code (NHTSA's vPIC lists none), that the number may be an Indian-assembled car, an import or a car built elsewhere, that the country is the code's and that the plant is not decoded

the reading of a WBA number names BMW AG, Germany; BMW's list note names WB3 (motorcycles by TVS) and says it is not read; Volvo's names MC2 (Volvo Eicher trucks) the same way; Audi's and Volvo's second codes (WA1, YV4) are read as their makers too

the guide lists the Indian codes and, apart, the international ones, and says that Audi, BMW, Volvo and BYD are different; vPIC is among its sources; the dropdown list scrolls (max height) so that twenty makers fit a screen

Fiat and Ford are in with their Indian codes (Fiat MAH, Ford MAJ), each with a remark that its new cars are no longer sold in India, said in the dropdown and in bold on the reading, with the dates and sources it rests on (Ford's statement of 9 Sep 2021, March 2025; Fiat's last cars 2019 to 2020 and no announced return in May 2026); no other maker has a remark

every reading answers the year and the month plainly: a year code at position 10 is YES (with the year and its other cycle year, said to be the MODEL year that may differ from the year built); a month is NO for every maker (the standard has no month field), except Hyundai with a plate stamp (YES, on the plate) and Hyundai without one (NO in these 17 characters, the stamp is said)

the card says it in bold, YES green and NO red, for both lines, under the heading 'Month and year of manufacture: is it in this number?', and shows the maker's remark in a bold red note; the dropdown marks Fiat and Ford 'No new cars sold in India now'
